visual_base.visual_narrative_log: (1) The video opens with a low-angle shot of a majestic Gothic-style cathedral in Kyiv. The structure is built from weathered grey stone, featuring intricate carvings of saints, pointed arches, and towering spires against a slightly overcast sky. The lighting is natural and diffuse, highlighting the architectural depth. (2) The scene shifts to a sunny public park where a man and a woman are walking two white samoyed dogs on leashes. They are dressed in casual outdoor clothing. Pigeons peck at the ground in the foreground while benches and bare spring trees line the pathway in the background. (3) A close-up shot features an elderly woman wearing a vibrant red puffer jacket sitting on a sidewalk. In front of her, trays of brown eggs and bundles of green onions are displayed for sale. She looks off-camera with a neutral expression as pigeons move around nearby on the pavement. (4) The scene transitions to an indoor interview setting. A man with short brown hair and glasses, wearing a dark blue blazer over a light-colored shirt, is seated in a plush red chair. He holds a yellow microphone with a 'Hahatai' logo and gestures with his right hand as he speaks. (5) A series of graphic overlays appear, showing a map of Ukraine colored to represent language distribution and bar charts comparing native language usage between 2022 and later periods. The background is a clean, neutral screen with prominent text and symbols. (6) Returning to the interview, the camera captures the man from a medium close-up angle. The background is softly blurred, showing a purple-lit wall and some interior decor. His facial expressions are engaged and serious as he explains his perspective, emphasizing points with subtle hand movements.
visual_base.text_narrative_log: (1) [Logo]: 哈哈台. [Slogan]: 烏克蘭/基輔 Ukraine/Kyiv. [Subtitle]: Ukraine and Russia are inseparably intertwined culturally. 在文化上的交織密不可分. (2) [Subtitle]: Identity is also complex. 身分認同也錯綜複雜. (3) [Subtitle]: Whether you speak Russian or Ukrainian has become a symbol of identity. 你說俄文還是烏克蘭文變成身分認同的象徵. (4) [Slogan]: Vitaliy Moroz/Ukrainian. [Subtitle]: Because Kyiv for years have been dominated by the Russian language. 因為多年來基輔一直由俄文主導. (5) [Subtitle]: Because Russia or the Soviet Union, they have been imposing their rules. 因為從蘇聯到現在的俄羅斯，他們總是要別人活在他們設下的框架裡. (6) [Subtitle]: And Russian was the main language. 讓俄文成為主要語言. (7) [Subtitle]: While I was always speaking Ukrainian, before I feel myself minority. 所以當我總是在說烏克蘭文的時候，以前我會感覺自己是少數. (8) [Subtitle]: But now, Russian language is associated with Russian as aggressor. 但現在俄文與俄羅斯作為侵略者的形象連結起來. (9) [Subtitle]: Many people, especially young people, have changed their attitude towards the language. 多人特別是年輕人，他們改變了對語言的態度. (10) [Subtitle]: They switched to Ukrainian and use it as the main language. 他切換成烏克蘭文並作為主要語言. (11) [Slogan]: 烏克蘭語言分布. [Logo]: 哈哈台. [Subtitle]: Before 2022, 30% of Ukrainians used Russian as their main language (mainly in the southeast). 烏克蘭在2022年前有3成的民眾以俄文為主要語言(主要集中在東南部). (12) [Subtitle]: 5成則以烏克蘭文為主. (13) [Subtitle]: After 2022, the number of Russian speakers has dropped significantly. 在2022年後俄文使用者大幅下降. (14) [Subtitle]: 80% of the population uses Ukrainian as their main language. 有8成民眾使用烏克蘭文為主要語言. (15) [Subtitle]: The switch in language has become a symbol of national identity. 語言的轉換成為民族認同的象徵. (16) [Subtitle]: Why you always speaking Ukrainian so long ago? 你很久以前為什麼決定要一直說烏克蘭文? (17) [Subtitle]: It is part of our identity. 這是我們身分認同的一部分. (18) [Subtitle]: Ukrainian means we are independent. 烏克蘭文意味著我們是獨立的. (19) [Subtitle]: We got our independence just 30 years ago, 1991. 我們獨立於1991年 30年前. (20) [Subtitle]: This means we departed from the Soviet Union which was another empire. 這意味著我們脫離了蘇聯. (21) [Subtitle]: with policy of colonialism towards other nation. 脫離了這個對其他國家有殖民主義的帝國. (22) [Subtitle]: And the Soviet Union never never acknowledge that republic has any choices. 而且蘇聯從未給過那些共和國任何選擇. (23) [Subtitle]: It was like 100 years ago, and it was always oppressed by Russians. 就像100年前，總是受到俄羅斯人的壓迫. (24) [Subtitle]: Since like the language is part of the identity, you just want to have this language which will not disappear. 由於語言是身分認同的一部分，你想要保有這個語言讓他不會消失. (25) [Subtitle]: Because all over the world, we have the situation. 因為在世界各地我們都有相同的情況. (26) [Subtitle]: When languages disappear because people stopped speaking these languages. 因為人們停止說這些語言所以這些語言消失了. (27) [Subtitle]: So if I speak Ukrainian and you speak Russian, we can easily understand each other. There's no need to change the languages. 舉例來說如果你說烏克蘭文你說俄文，我們可以很輕鬆地了解彼此，沒有必要轉換語言. (28) [Subtitle]: Our communication flows smoothly. 我們的溝通暢通無阻. (29) [Subtitle]: But speaking Ukrainian has always been a political manifestation. 但是說烏克蘭文一直都是一種政治上的表態. (30) [Subtitle]: For example, don't start speaking Russian just because your colleague does. 例如不要因為你的同事也說俄文你就開始說俄文.
